name: Real apply body honours gates and clamps
non_visual_rationale: A pure function's verdict inside the scoring engine. Nothing renders: build.ts still hands applyCorrection a literal null, so no published byte can move on this step at all. The observables are a returned gate token, a score delta and a member-height bias. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
delivered_over_two_commits: This step landed in two passes and the SECOND is what it delivers. c6237ed shipped the height lane UNCLAMPED: memberHBias returned the metres stored at a member's own (source, lead bucket) key with no bound on them. That approach was then rejected by an explicit decision, and this commit replaces it with an INERT height lane -- exactly zero metres for every model and every lead bucket -- proven by a new acceptance example and a new generated law. Every other criterion is unchanged from c6237ed and still green. Reason for the reversal: G5's forty-percent bound can only be taken where a member's own height is known, which is src/pipeline/build.ts, a file this lane must not touch. Shipping the metres ahead of their bound would leave the layer able to order an absurd wave height from the moment 02-03 wires a record in, on a product whose stated first rule is to never claim more certainty than the data earns. Zero is the day-zero forecast, which is never a lie. Nothing left this machine in between: the branch has never been pushed and build.ts still passes null, so no published byte ever moved through the unclamped body.
criteria_delivered: 1. applyCorrection(seed, record) re-checks n >= 10, reporters >= 5, abs(b) > 2*se from the record's OWN stated fields before applying anything. The stored `applied` boolean is never read; gateCorrection is imported from src/learning/gates.ts rather than restated, so apply and fit cannot drift apart and both anti-Sybil amendments are inherited with no new inputs.

2. applyCorrection(seed, null) still returns gate no_file, zero delta_q, zero member bias. tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts is byte-identical through this step and its R19 no-file identity law stays green as an independent fence.

3. DELIVERED AS AN INERT LANE, which is a stated refusal and not an untested gap. Every member is corrected by EXACTLY ZERO metres, whatever a record states at its key, because the metres and the 0.40-of-member-height clamp that bounds them may only ship together. The claim is tested rather than skipped: the acceptance example drives a record whose height key clears every rung on its own stated evidence and orders 0.60 m, and requires zero back; the generated law makes the same demand over 300 random records and carries a counter that fails the law outright if the generated space contained no key an unclamped body would have moved (measured: 18 such keys per 300 runs).
4. delta_q is MINUS the record's score b over 100, saturated at the record's own clamp.max_abs_score (12 display points as the emitter writes it). 06 section 4's sign, not 05 section 5's stale line.
5. combine keeps arity 3; no new parameter reaches the score path. Shipped scoring-laws R20 (combine.length === 3) stays green unchanged.
criteria_deferred: 3, in full. Neither half of 'corrected member is raw minus b per (source, lead bucket), clamped to 0.40 of the member height' ships. 05 section 5 pins the port at memberHBias(source, lead_h): two arguments, no height. The only production call site that knows a member's own height is src/pipeline/build.ts line 218, and this lane is under a standing instruction not to touch that file while a concurrent lane (f-see-what-killed-it phase 05, worktree /Users/andres/psb-deltas-slice0405) is actively modifying it. Widening memberHBias to take the height was considered and rejected: a required third parameter breaks build.ts's compile, and an optional one has no honest default. The two halves therefore land together, in the change that teaches this port the member's height and takes the fraction at the call site that knows it. NOT FLAGGED AS A WINDOW ANY MORE: there is no interval in which a height moves unbounded, because no height moves at all until the clamp arrives with it.
files_untouched_deliberately: src/pipeline/build.ts -- owned by a concurrent lane; git diff over both commits of this step names only the paths above.

tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts -- the feature-delta Test Reuse table marks its correction laws PRESERVE, and they are this step's independent fence. Byte-identical, and its R19 no-file identity law failed under the inert-lane mutation below, which is the fence doing its job.
harness_note: The accepted roadmap points this step at cucumber scenarios in a-correction-file-can-never-move-a-number-past-the-gates.feature and at a PENDING_SLICES entry. Neither exists on this branch; both live on recover/learning-build. Every committed acceptance step of this feature here proves its claim with one Vitest acceptance file, 1:1, and this step follows that shape. There was no skip marker to delete. The Vitest file's oracles were checked line by line against the authored .feature on recover/learning-build (git show f07943d:...): both forged scenarios there assert 'the waves AND score a surfer reads are exactly what day zero published', which is the whole-record verdict the oracles here encode -- and which an inert height lane satisfies exactly.
acceptance: Four named examples through applyCorrection. (1) A record forged to claim it was applied on six mornings is stopped and the outcome names n_lt_10. (2) A record forged to claim it was applied whose score difference is buried in its own stated error (se rewritten to 100) is stopped and names not_significant. (3) A record whose own stated evidence clears every rung moves the score by MINUS b/100 AND still moves no wave height at all, guarded against a vacuous pass by first asserting that the fixture's height key clears n >= 10, reporters >= 5 and abs(b) > 2*se on its own stated evidence with b != 0. (4) No file at all still returns no_file, zero, zero. Three of the four oracles reject a controlled doctored outcome of their own, and example 3 rejects two: a score delta with the wrong sign, and an outcome that subtracts the stored metres with no clamp on them. Every fixture is what buildCorrectionRecords actually emits for the stated mornings and people, not a hand-typed literal, so the claims are measured against the writer on the other side of the file.
unit_law: Four fast-check laws over generated records (200-300 runs each), with each key's stored `applied` boolean generated INDEPENDENTLY of the evidence beside it, which is exactly the shape a forged or stale file has. (a) A record claiming every key was applied and the same record claiming none produce byte-identical outcomes -- gate, score delta and every member bias. (b) The score moves only if the stated evidence behind it cleared the ladder. (c) The score move is MINUS the stored difference over 100 and never passes the limit the record itself states; max_abs_score is GENERATED rather than pinned to the shipped constant, so a body that hardcoded 12 is caught. (d) Every member is corrected by exactly zero metres, including at keys whose own evidence clears every rung, with the non-vacuity counter described under criteria_delivered 3. Plus one pinned example: a stored thirty-point move reaches the published score as twelve points.
generator_defect_found_and_fixed: The generators inherited from c6237ed drew b and se with fc.double over a bounded range. fc.double samples uniformly over the REPRESENTABLE doubles of that range, and representable doubles crowd around zero, so almost every draw landed within a rounding error of 0 and a stored height difference essentially never reached the region where its own ladder can clear. Measured, not assumed: with the fc.double generators the new inert law's counter reported ZERO keys whose evidence cleared the height ladder over 300 runs -- the law would have passed against an unclamped body for want of a case. Replaced with scaled integers (two decimals, the precision the emitter actually writes) at realistic magnitudes, and a height key's stated error now runs on the metre scale rather than the score's. The counter then reported 18 such keys per 300 runs and the law failed against the unclamped body on a shrunk counterexample. Laws (a) through (c) share those generators and are strictly stronger for the change; all stayed green.
design_decision_one_file_one_verdict: The score key is the record's verdict. It is the key a forged file moves a published score with, build.ts archives exactly one bias_gate per call, and the authored .feature says a refused file leaves 'the waves AND score' at day zero. So a file the score ladder refuses moves nothing at all. A record stating no score move at all states no evidence this body can weigh and is refused on the first rung, like any other file with too few mornings behind it. The per-key second gate that c6237ed ran on each height key is gone with the height lane it guarded, and returns with it.
declarations_trap: applyCorrection must name the gate that stopped a file, but src/learning/declarations.ts's whole-source examination flags the string literal 'applied' in any value position outside a file whose basename starts with `gates`. The token is therefore CARRIED: GateVerdict.reason was narrowed from `string` to a GateReason union in gates.ts (a type-only change, inside a type span, in the one privileged module) and engine.ts assigns `gate: verdict.reason`. No cast, no literal. PROVEN, not merely reasoned, in c6237ed: planting `gate: 'applied'` in engine.ts was run as a controlled mutation, and two acceptance tests that examine the REAL shipped tree (shipped-residual-inventory.test.ts and unreadable-correction-is-read-as-absent.test.ts, both rooted at src/ via import.meta.url, not at a synthetic tmp universe) failed with 'src/scoring/engine.ts can mark a correction applied without the gate having weighed the evidence'. Reverted; the tree is clean and both are green at this tip.
red_evidence: For the inert height lane, RED was observed against the SHIPPED unclamped body at c5de998 rather than against a stub, which is the strongest form available: the code that had to change was in the tree and the new assertions rejected it. Two failures, both semantic, zero collection errors, typecheck clean at RED so the red was behavioural. Acceptance: 'no member height may move until the forty-percent clamp can move with it: this record orders 0.5999999999999998 m at ncep_gfswave016 lead_24_48 and the apply body must subtract exactly zero, not 0.5999999999999998'. Unit, on a fast-check shrunk counterexample: 'ncep_gfswave016 at lead_24_48 must be corrected by exactly zero metres while G5's forty-percent clamp cannot bind, whatever the record states there (0.13 m on n=14, reporters=5, se=0)'. The other seven tests in the two files stayed green, which is the point: only the height lane changed. RED for criteria 1, 2, 4 and 5 was observed in c6237ed against the inert scaffold and is recorded in that commit's own evidence.
falsifiability_evidence: Three controlled mutations of the shipped body, each reverted, each failing semantically. (1) The inert height constant was made to return 0.01 m instead of 0: 6 tests failed across three files, including the new acceptance example ('must subtract exactly zero, not 0.01'), the new generated law, both forged examples on 'a file the gates refused must move the member height by exactly zero', and -- the independent fence -- shipped scoring-laws R19 on 'An absent correction file must contribute exactly zero member height bias, never an implicit prior'. (2) The score sign was flipped (`-bounded` -> `bounded`): 3 tests failed, including 'a stored difference of 4.5 display points must move the score by -0.01 ... it moved 0.01'. (3) The record's own score clamp was dropped: 2 tests failed, including 'the score move (-0.0646) must never pass the limit the record itself states (0.01)'. After all three reverts, `git status --short` names only the three paths this commit changes, tsc --noEmit exits 0 and the full suite is 409/409 across 82 files.
tests_changed_and_why: The two test files were committed by c6237ed and are modified here. This is a requirements change under an explicit decision, NOT a test weakened to fit an implementation, and the distinction is checkable: the assertions that changed became STRICTER, not looser. Where the acceptance oracle used to accept the stored metres it now demands exactly zero, and it gained a second doctored-outcome rejection proving it refuses an unclamped body. Where the generated law used to accept a per-key lookup it now demands zero at every key, and it gained a counter that fails the law if the generated space could not have caught the difference. One assertion was removed rather than tightened: law (b)'s height half, which asserted that a moved height implies cleared evidence, cannot be violated by a lane that moves nothing and would have been a permanently vacuous check; law (d) now owns the height claim outright. No production behaviour lost a test.
fixture_arithmetic: Measured, not assumed. Every observation in the fixture carries the same quality and the same shown score, so the sample standard error collapses to zero and the gate error is the physical floor alone. At 18 paired mornings from 6 people the emitter writes score_delta {b: 12.0, se: 2.946, n: 18, reporters: 6} -- |b| clears 2*se by better than twice over -- and a height key {b: 0.60, se: 0.0566, n: 18, reporters: 6}. Both clear every rung, which is what makes the inert height claim in acceptance example 3 non-vacuous: that record demonstrably orders a 0.60 m move and gets zero. At 6 mornings both keys refuse at n_lt_10, which is what the first forged example needs. The 30-point clamp example pins n: 30 deliberately: the G3 arithmetic is tight enough that a smaller sample count leaves a stored difference sitting close to twice its own floored error.
test_budget: Three behaviours in this step (the ladder is re-run from stated evidence; the score move's sign and its saturation; the height lane is inert). No-file identity and combine arity are pre-existing behaviours already fenced by shipped scoring-laws R19 and R20 and are not re-tested. Budget 2 x 3 = 6. Delivered: 4 acceptance examples (3 driven behaviours plus 1 preserved fence, 1:1 with the authored .feature scenarios this branch can reach) and 5 unit laws. Excluding the preserved fence, that is 8 tests against a budget of 6, stated plainly rather than rounded down. Net of this commit the count is unchanged from c6237ed's 7: law (b) lost its vacuous height half rather than a whole test, and no test was added or removed. The collapsible pair is still the thirty-point clamp example inside the sign-and-saturation property, which the generated law already covers over its whole range; it is kept because 12 display points is a stated product limit and a named example of it is worth one test. The second collapsible pair is acceptance example 3 against unit law (d), which make the same inert-height claim at two layers; they are kept apart because the acceptance example measures it against what the real emitter writes and the law measures it over the whole generated space.
scope_note: The roadmap lists three files_to_modify. tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts was deliberately NOT modified: its correction laws are marked PRESERVE and are this step's independent fence. One path outside the roadmap's list was touched (in c6237ed): src/learning/gates.ts, a two-line type-only narrowing of GateVerdict.reason to a GateReason union, which is what lets engine.ts carry the gate token instead of constructing it. That module is owned by this lane and the change is what the declarations examination requires; this commit does not touch it further. A fourth path, the step's own Vitest acceptance file, was added because this branch proves each step with a Vitest acceptance test rather than the cucumber scenario the roadmap names.
flagged_for_02_03_and_02_04: A record that states height keys but NO score move is refused as n_lt_10, because the ladder reads a key that states no evidence as a key with zero mornings behind it. That shape is reachable in production: a height residual needs a size band paired with a prediction, a score residual needs a quality word AND the score a build had shown the reporter, so a spot whose reporters never saw a forecast emits height keys and no score move. Such a record moves nothing, which is the honest and fail-closed outcome, but the token it is archived under names a morning count that is not the real reason. 02-03's criterion is that the archived call names the refusal reason, so the imprecision becomes operator-visible there. Flagged rather than fixed here: adding a fifth CorrectionGate token is a change to a shipped type that no test in this step drives, and the decision belongs with the step that archives the token.

The branch TIP does not, and the branch has never been pushed. Whether that intermediate commit should be squashed before this branch goes anywhere is the lane owner's call, not this step's. Nothing was lost -- the second pass began from the first's committed tree, and the full suite is green -- but two agents in one worktree is the condition the project's own rules forbid, and the lane owner should confirm a single writer before 02-03 starts.
